newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia probes rebel links after seizing guns.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia probes rebel links after seizing guns.

text.p: Indonesia said on Thursday it was investigating if foreigners had supplied 45 Russian- and U.S.-made rifles seized this week by the army in Aceh and believed to belong to rebels operating in the province.
Coordinating Minister for Political and Security Affairs Susilo Sudarman said the government was still conducting an investigation and so far it had not discovered any foreign links in the case.
"So far we haven't found any international link in this case," Sudarman told reporters after a monthly high-level security and political affairs meeting.

In an army operation this week in Aceh, on the northern tip of Sumatra island, 36 Russian-made AK-47 assault rifles and nine U.S.-made M-16 rifles were seized in two different intelligence raids. The rifles had been buried in plastic barrels.

The Kompas daily reported on Thursday that there was a firefight on Tuesday between soldiers and rebels in a village near Lhokseumawe, 1,600 km (992 miles) northwest of Jakarta, the main town nearest to where the guns were found.
Sudarman said AK-47s were not used by the Indonesian armed forces anymore and the M-16s must have been stolen by the rebels from the military.
He said the intelligence operation was conducted in Aceh after a recent bank robbery in Lhokseumawe where two people were killed by bandits using automatic rifles.
A separatist, mainly Islamic rebellion in Aceh peaked in 1990 and has now largerly subsided but few skirmishes between the rebels and the military are still reported.

Kompas quoted the north Sumatra military commander Major- General Sedaryanto as saying in Lhokseumawe on Wednesday that the seizure of the weapons was a strong indication the rebels were planning what he called a "comeback".
